2027-03-10.title: Fifth Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-03-10.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The end of those who walk away from God
2027-03-10.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-03-10.verse: Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.
theo: The little letter of Jude, tucked in just before the Book of Revelation, is one of the sternest pages of the New Testament. It was written against people inside the community who, Jude says, “defile the flesh, reject authority, and slander the glorious ones.” Yet in the middle of his rebuke he sets a strange example. Even the archangel Michael, when he “contended with the devil and disputed about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a condemnation of slander against him, but said, ‘The Lord rebuke you!’” If the greatest of the angels left judgment to God, how much more should we. Then Jude pours out images of a life that promises much and gives nothing: “These are blemishes on your love-feasts, while they feast with you without fear, feeding themselves. They are waterless clouds carried along by the winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted.” In March, when the heat lies heavy on Kerala, farmers look up at every cloud that gathers over the hills, hoping for the first summer shower; a cloud that passes without a drop is a bitter thing. Jude names three old figures of the way away from God: Cain, who killed his brother in envy; Balaam, who sold his gift for gain; Korah, who rebelled against the order God had given. Envy, greed and pride are still the roads by which a believer becomes a waterless cloud. The Great Fast asks: when people come to me, do they find rain, or only shade that passes? And Jude's own letter does not end in condemnation; a few verses later he tells the faithful to have mercy on those who waver, and to snatch others out of the fire.

The Gospel shows us how Jesus judges. Early in the morning, as he sits teaching in the temple, some scribes and Pharisees bring a woman “who had been caught in adultery; and making her stand before all of them,” they say: “Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery. Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such women. Now what do you say?” She is not a person to them but a trap; the man is nowhere to be seen. “Jesus bent down and wrote with his finger on the ground.” No one knows what he wrote; the Fathers remembered that the finger of God had once written the law on stone. When they press him, he stands and says: “Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.” And he bends down again. “When they heard it, they went away, one by one, beginning with the elders.” St Augustine said that in the end only two were left, misery and mercy (in substance). Then Jesus stands and speaks to her for the first time: “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” “No one, sir.” “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.” Mercy does not call sin nothing; it calls the sinner by name, lifts her up, and sends her into a new life. This is what happens in every confession of the Great Fast. We come holding the stones we wanted to throw at others, and we go away holding nothing but his word: go, and do not sin again.
outline: Ask: am I holding a stone for someone today?
A life that promises and does not give.
Jesus, the woman, and the stones laid down.
“Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
live: Name one person you have condemned in your heart or in your words, and pray for them by name today.
Make your Lenten confession this week if you have not yet done so, and hear the words: go, and do not sin again.
2027-03-10.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you bent down and wrote on the ground, and the stones fell from the hands of the accusers. Take from us every stone we hold against others, and save us from becoming waterless clouds and fruitless trees. Look on our misery with your mercy, call us by name, and send us out to begin again, never to return to our sin. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we stand where the woman stood, before the One who alone is without sin, and he does not condemn us but gives us himself as the food of a new life.

quick: Jude: even Michael left judgment to God; a life without fruit is a waterless cloud.
Jesus: let anyone without sin throw the first stone.
Mercy does not excuse sin; it lifts the sinner up and sends her into a new life.
2027-03-10.action: Put down one stone today: pray by name for someone you have condemned.
2027-03-10.question: Am I quicker to condemn others than to confess my own sin?

family.explain: Some men brought a woman to Jesus who had done something very wrong. They wanted to throw stones at her. Jesus said: whoever has never done anything wrong can throw the first stone. One by one they all went away, because everyone has done wrong things. Jesus told the woman: I do not condemn you; go, and do not do wrong again. Jesus forgives us too, and helps us to start again.
family.intention: We pray for all who will go to confession this Lent, that they may feel Jesus' mercy.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we have been angry with, whom we can forgive tonight?”

illus: In a family WhatsApp group in Thrissur a message arrived about a cousin whose marriage had broken down: a photo, a rumour, and a dozen comments within an hour. An elderly uncle who seldom wrote anything sent a single line: Let the one who has never sinned send the next message. The group went silent. That evening, instead of writing, he went to the cousin's house with a packet of jilebi from the bakery and sat with her for an hour, saying little. Months later she told her parish priest that his visit was the first time she had felt that God might still want her.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you do not condemn us but call us to a new life. Take the stones from our hands as we pray. Amen.
share: Waterless clouds carried along by the winds (Jude 12). Where do people find only a passing shadow in me, and no rain?
Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone (John 8:7). What stone am I holding?
Go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). What sin do I need to leave behind this Lent?
interc: For the Church, that she may always be a place of mercy that calls to conversion.
For priests who hear confessions in these weeks of the fast.
For those whose sins have been made public, and who are judged by many.
For families broken by betrayal, that they may find healing.
For our group, that we may put down our stones and pray for one another.
pm.close: Father of mercy, your Son stood between the sinner and the stones. Give us his heart, free us from condemning others, and bring us to a true conversion of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Jude reminds us that even the archangel Michael did not dare to condemn the devil, but said: the Lord rebuke you (Jude 9). Judgment belongs to God. And he warns us not to become waterless clouds and autumn trees without fruit (Jude 12): lives that promise and do not give.
In the temple some scribes and Pharisees bring Jesus a woman caught in adultery. They do not care for her; they want to trap him. Jesus bends down and writes on the ground.

Then he says: let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her (John 8:7). One by one they go away, beginning with the elders. Only two are left, as St Augustine says: misery and mercy.

Jesus tells her: neither do I condemn you; go your way, and from now on do not sin again (John 8:11). This is what happens in confession. This week, let us put down our stones, go to confession, and begin again. Amen.
kids: Children, some people wanted to throw stones at a woman who had done wrong. Jesus said: only someone who has never done wrong may throw a stone. Everyone went away! Jesus forgave her and said: go, and do not do wrong again. Jesus forgives us too when we say sorry.

intro: Theme: “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.”
The waterless clouds of Jude, the archangel who left judgment to God, and the meeting of misery and mercy in the temple.

sub: Trees that bear fruit in season.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
They are waterless clouds carried along by the winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, uprooted;
points.apply: Name one promise you made to God or to someone else this Lent, and keep it today.

sub: Michael did not dare to slander.
q: And the LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, O Satan! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is not this man a brand plucked from the fire?”
When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, “Let anyone among you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.”
points.apply: For one day, say nothing negative about anyone who is not present.

sub: Go, and do not sin again.
q: As I live, says the Lord GOD, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but that the wicked turn from their ways and live;
Neither do I condemn you. Go your way, and from now on do not sin again.
points.apply: Make your Lenten confession this week, and choose one concrete step away from your most frequent sin.

concl: Judgment belongs to God, who does not want the death of the sinner but his life.
Let us put down our stones, receive his mercy, and go out to sin no more.
2027-03-10.resolve: Go to confession before Hosanna Sunday, and pray each day this week for one person you have judged.
